topic: Curves: types and suitability, elements, geometry and setting out of curves (simple circular curve, vertical curve, transition curve)
source: survey 350-455 updated.json (merged from old LEVEL 7 archive)

questions.q: 413. The "point of curve" of a simple circular curve, is
questions.explain: The point of curve (PC) is the exact spot where the straight road ends and the circular curve begins, known as the point of commencement.

questions.q: 414. The "point of tangency" of a simple circular curve, is
options: the point where curve join the forward tangent
questions.explain: The point of tangency (PT) is specifically defined as the point where the curve ends and joins the forward tangent.

questions.q: 415. The central angle subtended by an arc of 30m of the curve
questions.explain: For a 30m arc, the degree of curve D is calculated as 1718.9/R (in minutes) based on the arc definition.

questions.q: 416. The length of perpendicular offset from a tangent to the junction of a transition curve and circular curve is equal to
questions.explain: The offset at the end of the transition curve (L) is mathematically equal to 4 times the shift (4S).

questions.q: 417. Find the length of curve if R=500 m, Intersection angle= 120°
questions.explain: Length L = (πRΔ)/180. Here Δ = 180-120 = 60°. So L = (3.1415 × 500 × 60)/180 ≈ 523.6m, rounding to 525m in the options.

questions.q: 418. Find the length of curve if radius of curve is 50 m and angle of deflection is 60°
419. Find the length of curve if radius of curve is 15 m and angle of deflection is 240°
questions.explain: L = (π × 15 × 240)/180 = 62.83m, which rounds to 63m.

questions.q: 420. The upgrade road meets with downgrade road then curve formed at the junction is called
questions.explain: When an upgrade meets a downgrade, it creates a convex profile (peak), which is a summit curve.

questions.q: 421. Overturning of vehicles on a curve can be avoided by using
questions.explain: A transition curve (spiral) gradually changes the radius from infinity to a fixed value, allowing centrifugal force to build up slowly and providing space to apply super-elevation, which prevents overturning.

questions.q: 422. A curve of varying radius introduced between two branches of a compound curve is called
questions.explain: When two arcs of a compound curve have significantly different radii, a transition curve is inserted between them to make the change in curvature gradual for the driver.

questions.q: 423. A transition curve introduced between the tangent and the circular curve should
options: have infinite curvature at the junction of straight and transition curve
have zero curvature at the junction of straight and transition curve
questions.explain: At the start (tangent point), the transition curve must have zero curvature (infinite radius) to perfectly match the straight path.

questions.q: 424. A curve consists of two areas of different radii bending in the same direction and lying on the same side of their common tangent and their centers being on the same side of the curve is known as a
questions.explain: A compound curve is defined specifically as two (or more) circular arcs of different radii that turn in the same direction and share a common tangent.

questions.q: 425. Different grades are joined together by a
questions.explain: Vertical curves (parabolic curves) are specifically designed to smoothly connect two different gradients (grades) to prevent an abrupt bump or dip in the road.

questions.q: 426. Cubic parabola is a type of
questions.explain: The cubic parabola is a specific mathematical curve where the offset is proportional to the cube of the distance, making it a very common form for transition curves in railway engineering.

questions.q: 427. If the length of a transition curve is such that the full super elevation is attained at the junction with the circular curve, the resultant curve is known as
questions.explain: In this specific classification from the source key, the resulting combined geometry is referred to as a compound curve system.

questions.q: 428. The angle subtended by the long chord of a simple curve at its centre is equal to
questions.explain: According to circle geometry, the angle at the center is exactly twice the deflection angle (2 × delta).

questions.q: 429. The chord of curve less than peg interval is known as
questions.explain: The technical term in surveying for this is a 'sub-chord.' Since 'sub-chord' isn't listed, 'none of the above' is the technical answer according to the key.

questions.q: 430. The Normal chord of a curve should be
questions.explain: A normal chord is the full standard length of a chain or tape (like 20m or 30m), whereas a sub-chord is a fractional piece used to finish the curve; thus, the normal chord is always greater than the sub-chord.

questions.q: 431. The shape of the vertical curve generally used is:
questions.explain: Parabolic curves are preferred for vertical alignment because they provide a constant rate of change of grade, which ensures a smooth transition for vehicles.

questions.q: 432. The angle of intersection of a curve is the angle between:
questions.explain: The angle of intersection (I) is the angle specifically measured between the back tangent and the forward tangent at the point of intersection (PI).

questions.q: 446. Combination of two reverse curve is a:
questions.explain: A deviation curve is used to bypass an obstacle and return to the original path; it is essentially a combination of two reverse curves.
